examples.en: My uncle answered in a cold tone.

examples.ko: 싸운 뒤로 집 안 분위기가 냉랭해요.
examples.en: Since the fight, the mood at home has been frosty.
The boss's face was cold from the morning, which was scary.

examples.ko: 두 사람 사이가 냉랭해진 지 오래됐어요.
examples.en: It has been a long time since the two grew cold toward each other.
I greeted them, but the response was cold.
I was hurt by the cold attitude.

explain: 온도보다 분위기, 말투, 표정, 사이가 차가울 때 많이 써요. '쌀쌀하다'는 날씨에도 쓰지만 '냉랭하다'는 주로 사람 쪽 이야기에 어울리고, 반대로는 '다정하다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for a cold mood, tone, expression or relationship rather than temperature. '쌀쌀하다' also works for weather, but '냉랭하다' suits talk about people, and the opposite is '다정하다'.

en: stream of water; jet of water

examples.en: A stream of water pours down the mountain.
The water from the shower is too weak.
The firefighter sprayed a jet of water at the fire.
The course of this river runs all the way to the sea.
The sound of the waterfall is very loud.
The gardener sprays a thin stream of water on the flowers.

explain: 이름이 있는 큰 흐름은 '강'이고, 수도꼭지·호스·폭포에서 가늘고 길게 나오는 물에도 '물줄기'를 써요. '물줄기가 세다/약하다', '물줄기를 뿜다'처럼 말해요. 강이 흘러가는 길을 말할 때는 '물길'도 써요.
explain_en: A big named flow is a '강', but '물줄기' is also used for the thin, long line of water from a faucet, a hose or a waterfall. You say '물줄기가 세다/약하다' and '물줄기를 뿜다'. For the path a river takes, '물길' is also used.

examples.en: I walked down a road where cosmos swayed in the autumn breeze.
The puppy greeted me, wagging its tail.
The wind chime by the window tinkled lightly and woke me up.
Now that spring is here, the willow branches sway gently.

examples.ko: 열어 둔 창문 때문에 커튼이 밤새 살랑댔어요.
examples.en: Because I left the window open, the curtain swayed all night.
Every time the breeze stirs, I smell the flowers.

explain: '살랑거리다'와 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 활용이 '살랑대요, 살랑댔어요, 살랑대는'처럼 짧고 간단해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '살랑거리다' and can replace it. Its conjugations are short and simple: '살랑대요', '살랑댔어요', '살랑대는'.

examples.en: When spring came, new shoots sprouted on every tree.
New shoots are very tender, so they get damaged easily.

examples.ko: 새순을 따서 나물로 무쳐 먹기도 해요.
examples.en: People sometimes pick the young shoots and season them as a side dish.
One new shoot came up in the flowerpot.
It's March, but I can't even see new shoots yet.

examples.ko: 새순에 물을 너무 많이 주지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't give the new shoots too much water.

explain: '새싹'은 씨에서 처음 올라온 싹이고, '새순'은 이미 있는 줄기나 가지에서 새로 나온 어린 순이에요. 그래서 큰 나무나 오래된 화분에는 '새순'이 더 자연스러워요. '새순이 돋다', '새순이 나다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '새싹' is the first sprout from a seed, while '새순' is a young shoot growing from an existing stem or branch. So '새순' feels more natural for big trees or old plants. It goes with '새순이 돋다' and '새순이 나다'.

examples.ko: 아이는 들고 있던 조약돌을 멀리 던졌어요.
examples.en: The child threw the pebble he was holding far away.
Round pebbles are spread along the stream.
Pebbles are smooth because water has washed them for a long time.
I put one pebble in my pocket and came back.
You have a round face like a pebble on the beach.
I made a path with pebbles in the garden.

explain: 냇가나 바닷가에서 볼 수 있는 작고 동글동글한 돌이에요. '자갈'은 여러 개가 깔려 있는 작은 돌을 말할 때가 많고, '조약돌'은 매끈하고 둥근 모양이 먼저 떠올라요. 아이들이 줍거나 던지고 노는 장면에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a small round stone you find by streams and beaches. '자갈' often refers to many small stones spread out, while '조약돌' brings to mind the smooth, round shape. It often appears in scenes of children picking up or throwing stones.

examples.ko: 타조는 날지 못하지만 아주 빨리 달려요.
examples.en: Ostriches cannot fly, but they run very fast.
I saw an ostrich for the first time at the zoo.

examples.ko: 타조 알은 닭 알보다 훨씬 커요.
examples.en: An ostrich egg is much bigger than a chicken egg.
The children gave food to the ostrich.
Some people raise ostriches on farms.
The ostrich strode away on its long legs.

explain: 날지 못하는 새로는 펭귄도 있지만, 펭귄은 헤엄치고 타조는 땅에서 달려요. 새와 동물은 '한 마리, 두 마리'로 세요. '타조 알', '타조 고기'처럼 뒤에 다른 말을 붙여 쓸 때가 많아요.
explain_en: Penguins also cannot fly, but a penguin swims while a 타조 runs on land. Birds and animals are counted with 마리, as in 한 마리, 두 마리. 타조 often takes a word after it, like 타조 알 (ostrich egg) and 타조 고기 (ostrich meat).

en: make sprout; put out (shoots); clear (a path)

examples.en: When spring comes, the seeds sprout.
I tried sprouting beans on the balcony.

examples.ko: 저는 화분에 해바라기 싹을 틔우고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to get a sunflower to sprout in a pot.
I'm waiting until the tree puts out new shoots.

examples.ko: 이 씨앗은 물에 불리면 싹을 더 빨리 틔워요.
examples.en: If you soak these seeds, they sprout faster.
Thank you for clearing the blocked waterway.

explain: '싹이 트다'는 싹이 스스로 나올 때, '싹을 틔우다'는 씨앗이나 사람이 싹을 내는 쪽에서 말해요. 발음은 [티우다]예요. 막힌 길이나 물길을 열어 줄 때도 쓰지만 일상 대화에서는 주로 싹과 함께 나와요.
explain_en: '싹이 트다' is used when a sprout comes out by itself, while '싹을 틔우다' looks at it from the seed or the person making it sprout. It is pronounced [티우다]. It can also mean opening a blocked path or waterway, but in daily talk it mostly appears with sprouts.
